task.goal: Produce one slide of a 'juxtaposition reaction' comparison-meme carousel (flat two-figure stick-character format) that lands a single wanted-vs-reality contrast beat, in the reduced pink/black visual language this format is recognized by.
task.success_condition: The slide reads correctly at a glance on mobile: the left figure unambiguously registers as the idealized/desired subject and the right ('me') figure unambiguously registers as the deflecting reaction; the two text labels are the sole carriers of meaning since the figures themselves are visually identical slide to slide; and if the slide is sponsored or CTA-driven, that is disclosed in-frame rather than blended in as an organic beat.
task.atomic_boundary: One source comparison premise becomes one slide. This harness governs a single juxtaposition-beat slide unit, not the full multi-slide carousel arc, sequencing, or outer caption copy.

source_expression_moment.description: The comparison premise for this slide, expressed as the two opposed labels to render (e.g. 'my ex' vs 'me', 'good grades' vs 'me').

voice_context.description: Tone/voice reference for the label copy — dry, self-deprecating, deadpan; no exclamation-driven or hard-sell phrasing.

carousel_slide.description: One production-ready square (1:1) slide image: two stick figures on a flat single-color ground, each with a bold label caption, composed per this format's visual syntax.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer scrolls past this exact 'X vs me' template constantly; the only thing that can still land is the specific unfairness/pettiness of the comparison itself, not the illustration, which never changes.
stakes: the joke reads as generic instead of specific
a sponsored slide gets mistaken for an organic confession and damages trust when noticed
identity_urges: see my own pattern named accurately
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer reads both labels, recognizes the specific comparison as their own behavior, and reacts (laugh, share, tag someone). No explicit call-to-action on non-sponsored slides.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer self-identifies with the 'me' figure for this specific comparison and finds it funny rather than judgmental.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Tag or send the slide to whoever else it applies to.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not let the stick-figure poses or expressions carry format-specific meaning beyond generic affection-vs-rejection — the figures are visually near-identical slide to slide, so the entire comedic payload lives in the two text labels; ambiguous, unopposed, or non-parallel label pairs collapse the format.

Do not caption both figures with the same valence, or leave one uncaptioned — the left figure must always read as the wanted/idealized party and the right ('me') as the deflecting party, or the reversal reads as a random illustration instead of a self-aware joke.

Do not deploy this exact template for sponsored or CTA-driven content without an explicit, in-frame paid-partnership disclosure — the format's stripped-down 'personal confession' visual language makes it easy for a promoted slide to be misread as authentic, unsponsored commentary.

Do not introduce texture, photography, gradients, or a multi-color ground — the format's recognizability depends on a flat single-color background with black linework figures; adding texture reads as a different (photo-comparison) format entirely.

Do not hard-code romantic jealousy as the only valid label pairing — the underlying format is a general wanted-vs-reality comparison beat (exes, grades, apps, habits, etc.); over-narrowing the harness to jealousy-only content would misclassify the format's actual native range.
wrong_reading_locks_meaning: Do not treat jealousy as a moral failing -- PRM-HUM-009 re-frames it as a diagnostic compass for hidden desire.
Do not prescribe immediate action on slide 1 -- EXP-FBK-004 requires progression through recognition before commitment.
